results.content:
# BDR names Ryan Farris as new Chief Executive Officer  
*Founder Bruce Wiseman to move into role of executive chairman role as company strengthens its leadership team for long-term growth.*  
SEATTLE – July 14, 2026 – Business Development Resources (BDR), the premier provider of business coaching, training and marketing services for home service contractors across North America, announces the appointment of Ryan Farris as chief executive officer, effective today. BDR founder Bruce Wiseman will remain with the company, transitioning into the role of Executive Chairman.  
“One of the most important responsibilities of any founder is ensuring the organization is positioned for long-term success,” said Wiseman. “After an extensive search process, I am confident we found the right leader in Ryan. I know he will serve BDR with integrity, humility, and a deep appreciation for the culture that makes this company so special.  
Farris joins BDR with more than 30 years of leadership experience spanning entrepreneurship, technology, marketing and business operations. After more than a decade in corporate leadership, he founded and built his own company before successfully exiting the business. That entrepreneurial journey sparked a passion for helping fellow business owners succeed.
For the past 10 years, Farris has dedicated his career to partnering with entrepreneurs and small business owners, providing coaching, training and strategic support that helps them create sustainable growth. His experience and passion closely align with BDR’s mission of helping home service contractors become “Prime”—the very best they can be in every aspect of their business and leadership.  
“From my very first conversations with the team, it was clear BDR is a very special company,” said Farris. “What the team has built over nearly three decades is remarkable. I’m honored to lead this outstanding company at such an exciting point in its journey, and I look forward to building on its strong foundation, expanding BDR’s reach, and helping even more home service business owners build stronger, more profitable businesses.”  
Founded in 1998 by Wiseman and Barry Burnett, BDR has grown into a nationally recognized brand, supporting home services contractors, distributors, and platform companies in driving profit and growth in their businesses. With thousands of companies leveraging industry-leading best practices, marketing execution, accounting and financial support, and team member training resources every month, BDR has become the go-to business enablement resource across the trades.
“From the beginning, Barry, Kim Archer, and myself set out to help contractors build a more successful business. Almost 30 years later, that mission still remains true,” said Wiseman. “While my title might be changing, my commitment to BDR won’t as I continue to work with our leadership team, our clients, and our partners to build on the strong foundation we’ve created together.”

results.name: The 10 best AI BDRs in 2026
results.content:
# The 10 best AI BDRs in 2026  
What an AI BDR must own end to end, and the 10 outbound-capable platforms ranked against that bar, with pricing and fit guidance.  
[Jaspar Carmichael-Jack](https://www.artisan.co/authors/jaspar-carmichael-jack)16 minutes readJul 24, 2026
Artisan's Ava is the best AI BDR (business development representative) in 2026: she is the only agent that owns every stage of the outbound job (sourcing, enrichment, multichannel outreach, reply handling, and booking) inside one platform, with autonomy you dial up or down. AiSDR and Amplemarket are the strongest alternatives. Most other tools cover part of the job.  
A BDR's job is outbound pipeline generation, nothing else. So this guide, updated July 2026, does something different from the usual listicle. It defines the AI BDR category, breaks the outbound job into the five stages an AI BDR must own, and ranks only outbound-capable platforms against one question: can it actually do the whole job?
## What changed in the AI BDR category in 2025-2026?  
- **Apollo bought Pocus**(March 19, 2026), pushing the biggest per-seat platform toward an "AI-native GTM OS" and signal-driven selling.
- **Salesforce closed its Qualified acquisition**(April 1, 2026), consolidating inbound agents into Agentforce and sharpening the inbound/outbound split this article ranks on.
- **11x reset its leadership**after TechCrunch's March 2025 reporting on misstated customers. CTO Prabhav Jain became CEO in May 2025.
- **New money chased the autonomous end:**Alta's $25 million Series A (July 8, 2026) and Monaco's $50M Series B led by Benchmark (May 2026) both back agents, not seat software.
- **Pricing moved toward usage and outcomes:**Salesforce shifted Agentforce to $0.10/action Flex Credits and HubSpot launched credit-based outcome pricing ($0.010 per credit) in April 2026. The market is converging on paying for work performed.
